citation: This work (UniProt Q9C5C0 motif scan, 20 AtMPKs + ERK2/p38/JNK1)
claim: Every catalytic element of the kinase fold is intact in MPK18
finding: G-loop GKGSYG 32-37; VAIK K54; HRD D151 (HRDLKPKN 149-156); DFG D169; activation loop TDY 187-189; APE 197-199. 6/6 canonical, 0 substitutions. Paralog MPK17 carries DLG, showing the scan detects substitutions.
confidence: High for motif presence. Sequence cannot establish activity.

claim: MPK18 folds into an active-competent kinase
finding: Kinase domain 25-310 pLDDT 89.5. K54 NZ to E72 CD 3.52 A (alphaC-in ion pair); D151-K153 3.44 A; D151-N156 3.30 A; P-loop to DFG 12.89 A. T187/Y189 pLDDT 49/48, consistent with an unphosphorylated flexible activation loop.
confidence: High pLDDT in the kinase domain. A prediction, not an assay; AlphaFold is biased toward active-like kinase conformations.

citation: This work (20 AtMPKs; replicated in 18 rice and moss MAPKs)
claim: MPK18 is TDY group D and lacks the canonical CD docking site
finding: TDY in exactly the 8 Arabidopsis group D members, TEY in all 12 others. CD window: MPK18 LSKIEREPS net 0 vs ERK2 YYDPSDEPI +3 and MPK6 LHDISDEPE +4. Arabidopsis TEY +2.38 vs TDY +0.38 (U=58, p=0.0029, r=+0.81). Rice replicate: TEY +2.43 vs TDY +0.36 (U=72, p=0.00082, r=+0.87); tails 352 vs 165 aa (p=0.00028).
confidence: High and cross-species replicated. The CD window is a proxy, not a measured docking affinity.

claim: DEF-pocket divergence could independently argue MPK18 lacks substrates
finding: NEGATIVE CONTROL. MPK18 V236/V237/L240/Y266 vs ERK2 Y233/L234/L237/Y263. MPK3 (H/V/M/Y) and MPK6 (H/V/L/I, zero aromatic) are equally or more diverged yet have known substrates.
confidence: High. Rules out DEF divergence as a discriminating argument.

claim: The microtubule phenotype is attributed to MPK18 kinase activity
finding: It is not. Y2H and BiFC with PHS1 in the cytoplasm; PHS1 dephosphorylates phospho-MPK18 in vitro; mpk18 T-DNA has moderately stabilised microtubules; mpk18 partially suppresses phs1-1 roots. No kinase-dead rescue, no MPK18 kinase assay, no substrate. Framed as 'We propose a model'.
context: Arabidopsis seedlings, roots; yeast; in vitro
confidence: Moderate. Loss of function plus a phosphatase partner; MPK18 assayed only as a phosphoacceptor.

finding: MKKK20, a MAP3K, phosphorylates MPK18 directly in vitro. MKK3 does not interact with MPK18, and adding all three kinases gives no synergy. mkkk20 and mkk3 roots are short on microtubule drugs, assigned to two non-complementary pathways.
context: Arabidopsis; in vitro kinase assay, Y2H, BiFC, root phenotype
confidence: Moderate to high for the negative MKK3 result. In vitro phosphorylation may not reflect in planta activation.

claim: MKK3 is the MAP2K for TDY group D MAPKs
finding: MKK3 phosphorylates and activates MPK8, with calmodulin required for full activation. Establishes the clade prior that MPK18 data then contradict.
confidence: High for MPK8. Does not transfer to MPK18.

claim: MPK18 kinase activity drives the PHS1-linked microtubule phenotype
finding: PHS1 has its own Mn-dependent atypical kinase domain that phosphorylates alpha-tubulin Thr349 and depolymerises microtubules. In the phs1 null, stress-induced depolymerisation does not occur. MPK18 is not involved.
confidence: High. Gives an MPK18-independent mechanism for microtubule remodelling by PHS1.

claim: Interactome data nominate an MPK18 substrate class
finding: MPK18 binds DELLA proteins GAI, RGA, RGL2 and BREVIS RADIX in binary Y2H maps. Untargeted screens, no phosphorylation shown.
confidence: Low for substrate assignment. Weak lead only.

claim: A plant MAPK substrate screen covers MPK18
finding: The protein-microarray screen profiled 10 MPKs and found 570 substrates. MPK18 was not among the profiled kinases, which is why no substrate set exists for it.
confidence: High. Explains the gap rather than filling it.
